video_title: Boogie & Chandler On Mavs New Head Coach Dusty May!

quotes.speaker: DeMarcus Cousins
quotes.summary_phrase: DeMarcus Cousins on why Kawhi Leonard won't take a pay cut
quotes.excerpt: When it comes down to situations of money and you haven't won a championship for an organization, I have a hard time seeing him saying, 'I'm willing to take less so you guys can go make other moves.'
quotes.quote: This is a two-time NBA champion. He's seen it all, he's done it all, he feels accomplished. He's done everything he can do besides win another championship, but he's already done it. So when it comes down to situations of money and you haven't won a championship for an organization, I have a hard time seeing him saying, 'I'm willing to take less so you guys can go make other moves,' especially with the climate and seeing how everybody is moving around and people are trying to find their way to what their next situation is going to be and what's going to be the best opportunity for themselves. I'm curious to see what Kawhi's decision is. I don't think he's going to take a pay cut to stay there if there's a way that they can figure out the money part. I think he's happy with the Clippers, but if it comes down to money and taking less for somebody else, I don't see it happening.

quotes.speaker: Chandler Parsons
quotes.summary_phrase: Chandler Parsons on why Kawhi Leonard shouldn't take a pay cut
quotes.excerpt: He's also coming off a fantastic year where he's gone through a bunch of injuries, more so than most players in the NBA.
quotes.quote: At this point of his career, he's 34 years old. He's also coming off a fantastic year where he's gone through a bunch of injuries, more so than most players in the NBA, and still is playing at an elite level. But he's also made a lot of money. So would it make sense for Boston to do that, a competitive team that actually can compete for a championship? Maybe. But I'm with Boogie, there's no reason this dude should take a pay cut to go back to the Clippers. And even the other options, whether it's the Warriors or the Heat, realistically those aren't championship rosters right now. Now, a lot can happen in the draft and free agency, but those three teams I keep hearing his name surrounding don't really deserve a pay cut in my opinion.

quotes.speaker: DeMarcus Cousins
quotes.summary_phrase: DeMarcus Cousins on Draymond Green's future with the Warriors
quotes.excerpt: I can see Draymond riding off in the sunset, returning with the group he started with.
quotes.quote: I'm not buying that this is his final year with the Warriors. I think they'll figure out something down the line, something suitable for Draymond and the team, something that makes sense for both sides. I can see Draymond riding off in the sunset, returning with the group he started with. It only makes sense. Obviously, you think about the group that came in and you think about guys like Klay. It didn't work out, unfortunately, it didn't work out the way it should have with him riding off in the sunset as well. So I think they make the right decision with Draymond and they just figure things out.

quotes.speaker: Chandler Parsons
quotes.summary_phrase: Chandler Parsons on Draymond Green as a Warrior for life
quotes.excerpt: I think him, Steph Curry, and Steve Kerr, I think they ride into the sunset together.
quotes.quote: I think he's a Warrior for life. I really do. I think his position stays there. Maybe go somewhere with LeBron, they have a really close relationship and maybe they find a way to get that done with their connection with Rich Paul and things like that. But I just don't see it. I think him, Steph Curry, and Steve Kerr, I think they ride into the sunset together. I think it makes the most sense for him to stay put there where he's always been. It's still weird to be that Klay is on the Mavs.

quotes.speaker: DeMarcus Cousins
quotes.summary_phrase: DeMarcus Cousins on Lu Dort's defensive value to the Lakers
quotes.excerpt: You go in and get an elite level 3-and-D guy like a Lu Dort, that's what he does.
quotes.quote: I don't mind it. Lakers got plenty of scoring and what was their Achilles heel this year? We constantly were talking about them on the defensive end, whether they're strong enough on the defensive end to compete in the Western Conference. So you go in and get an elite level 3-and-D guy like a Lu Dort, that's what he does and that's what he takes pride in. I think that gives the Lakers a good look. I'm in the same world with the OKC Thunder with Lu Dort as I am with Draymond Green. I've gotten so accustomed to seeing him with that group, I can't see him anywhere else. But if the Lakers decided that they wanted to get better on the defensive end, Lu Dort would be a tremendous start for them.

quotes.speaker: Chandler Parsons
quotes.summary_phrase: Chandler Parsons on Lu Dort as a perfect fit for the Lakers
quotes.excerpt: I think he's exactly what the Lakers need in 3-and-D, space the floor, have someone make up that defensive slack.
quotes.quote: This is interesting because I think it works perfect for both sides. I think he's exactly what the Lakers need in 3-and-D, space the floor, have someone make up that defensive slack for Luka and Austin Reaves if they do give Austin the big extension. And then for the Oklahoma City Thunder, you see they already made moves yesterday trading Aaron Wiggins, but they still have Cason Wallace, they still have Jalen Williams, they still have AJ Mitchell. Just feels like this postseason run for them, Lu Dort was going to be the odd man out this summer because now I think there's really more of an emphasis on re-signing Isaiah Hartenstein. I think he's more valuable with the play of Chet in this offseason to re-acquire him in free agency. So I do think Lu Dort is the odd man out.

quotes.speaker: DeMarcus Cousins
quotes.summary_phrase: DeMarcus Cousins on the importance of Shai Gilgeous-Alexander to Lu Dort
quotes.excerpt: I don't think this guy is on the move and I think it's one thing we're kind of overlooking.
quotes.quote: I don't think this guy is on the move and I think it's one thing we're kind of overlooking and that's his relationship with Shai. These are two guys that are from the same country, both Canadian. They kind of came in the game together, they've grown together over the years, they've won championships over the years. So I think Shai plays a huge part in that as far as voicing his opinion with keeping a guy like Lu Dort on the team. So I think OKC figures it out for both sides and he continues on with the Thunder.

quotes.speaker: Chandler Parsons
quotes.summary_phrase: Chandler Parsons on Dusty May's potential as Mavericks head coach
quotes.excerpt: I like the youth, I like the way that he'll be able to coach and relate to Cooper Flagg.
quotes.quote: Listen, he's killed it in the college ranks. He started off from the bottom and now he obviously you see what he's done winning a national championship. I don't know the guy, I like the youth, I like the way that he'll be able to coach and relate to Cooper Flagg and that young team. Is he an experienced championship-level coach to win now in the NBA? No, but neither was JJ Redick, neither were a lot of these guys that are just hired with not that experience. This guy's had a ton of experience in the college ranks, so wow, that's crazy. I didn't see that happen.

quotes.speaker: DeMarcus Cousins
quotes.summary_phrase: DeMarcus Cousins on Dusty May's ability to connect with young players
quotes.excerpt: Trying to connect with young players and bringing in new talent and somebody with fresh ideas and philosophies.
quotes.quote: I don't know much about him as a person or as a coach. I know he just won the natty, but again, trying to connect with young players and bringing in new talent and somebody with fresh ideas and philosophies to try to help these young stars and help the Dallas Mavericks get back on track. Much love to Dusty.

quotes.speaker: Chandler Parsons
quotes.summary_phrase: Chandler Parsons on Dusty May's coaching style
quotes.excerpt: He's fun, he's exciting, he's innovative, he runs a great offense.
quotes.quote: He's been around for a while. He's fun, he's exciting, he's innovative, he runs a great offense. He just won a championship, right, at Michigan this past year. So it feels like this is just like a complete young start, like everything's going to be fresh, everything's going to be on. It seems like it's trying to get on the same timeline as that young stud in Cooper Flagg. You bring in a fresh face, a new coach to this system, bringing his own new system in. I think it works perfectly, honestly, so it makes sense.
